change.title: pr-37038-flat
change.description: Add Groups resource type and scopes to authorization schema
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: canManage() grants manage to admins that only have VIEW on all groups
findings.body: `canManage()` returns true when `hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)` matches, so an all-groups permission with only the `view` scope passes `requireManage()`. `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` (GroupsResource.java:181) uses only `auth.groups().requireManage()`, which means a view-only admin can create top-level groups and move existing groups to the top level. The interface Javadoc (GroupPermissionEvaluator.java:72-77) repeats the same VIEW/MANAGE wording. Change the check to `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, the same as `canManage(GroupModel)` at line 79, and add a test that a VIEW-only all-groups admin gets 403 on POST /groups.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authz resource IDs, not group IDs
findings.body:
In V2, `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` creates the resource with name = group id (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:109,121). Its `getId()` is a generated authz UUID. This loop passes `groupResource.getId()` to `hasPermission`, which looks the resource up with `findByName` (line 141). It also adds `getId()` to the result set. So the lookup never finds the group resource and falls back to the all-groups resource, and the returned IDs are not group IDs. V1 uses `resource.getName()` here (GroupPermissions.java:315).

Callers pass this set as the group filter to `UsersResource.getUsersCount` (UsersResource.java:398,425,430) and set it as `UserModel.GROUPS` for the search (UsersResource.java:448-450, BruteForceUsersResource.java:147-149). An admin who can see users only through group view-members gets a wrong count, or an empty or wrong search result, with no error. Use `groupResource.getName()` in both places.

I could not confirm that `findByType(server, "Groups", ...)` returns the per-group resources. `create(server, name, owner)` does not appear to set a type. If it doesn't, this method always returns an empty set, and the count endpoint is wrong either way. The tests only cover the list endpoint, where `toRepresentation` filters each user with `canView` again.

findings.title: requireManageMembers Javadoc points to the wrong method
findings.body: The Javadoc for `requireManageMembers` says it throws when `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` is false. It should name `canManageMembers(GroupModel)`. Also, `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission`'s `@return` (line 145) says "Stream", but the method returns a `Set`.

contracts.action: POST /groups by an admin whose all-groups permission has only the VIEW scope
contracts.before_after: addTopLevelGroup calls requireManage() first and then creates or moves the group
contracts.visible_effect: The group is created when the request should get 403
contracts.failure_mode: Privilege escalation from view to manage

contracts.action: Users count/search filtered by the group IDs from getGroupIdsWithViewPermission (V2)
contracts.before_after: UsersResource passes the set to getUsersCount and to the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute
contracts.visible_effect: Wrong user count or search page for an admin who sees users through groups
contracts.open_question: Does findByType(server, "Groups") return the per-group resources, given that create() does not seem to set a type?

summary: This PR adds the V2 FGAP Groups resource type. I found one blocker. In V2, `canManage()` accepts the VIEW scope, so a view-only all-groups admin can create top-level groups. Separately, the V2 `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` collects authz resource IDs where it should use group IDs (the resource name), which skews user counts and searches for admins who see users through groups. One Javadoc names the wrong method.
